name: eridu-settled-sumer
description: Farmers settled the marshy southern plain at Eridu, which Sumerians later remembered as the oldest city of their land.

name: uruk-first-city-walled
description: Uruk grew into a walled urban centre with great temples and thousands of residents, the largest settlement of its day.

name: cuneiform-writing-emerges
description: Scribes pressed wedge-shaped marks into wet clay tablets to record grain, beer and temple goods, the first writing.

name: royal-tombs-of-ur
description: Rulers of a Sumerian city were buried with lyres, gold headdresses and attendants in richly furnished underground tombs.

name: urukagina-reforms-lagash
description: A Sumerian king curbed corrupt officials and protected widows and the poor in what is often called the first recorded reform.

name: enheduanna-hymns-inanna
description: A priestess and daughter of a king composed hymns to the goddess Inanna, becoming the first author known by name.

name: naram-sin-victory-stele
description: A king showed himself climbing a mountain over fallen enemies and took the title King of the Four Quarters.

name: elamites-sack-ur
description: Raiders from the east captured the city and carried off its king, ending the last great Sumerian dynasty.

name: amorite-dynasty-babylon
description: A chieftain founded a ruling house in a small river town that would grow into the most famous city of Mesopotamia.

name: plimpton-322-tablet
description: A clay tablet lists number sets that match right triangles, showing advanced mathematics long before the Greeks.

name: code-of-hammurabi-carved
friendly_name: The Code of Hammurabi Is Carved
description: Nearly three hundred laws, including an eye for an eye, were inscribed on a black stone pillar for all to read.

name: hittites-sack-babylon
description: A raiding army from Anatolia plundered the capital and carried off the statue of its chief god, ending its famous dynasty.

name: ashur-uballit-frees-assyria
description: An Assyrian king wrote to the pharaoh as an equal and freed his city from Mitanni overlordship, starting an empire.

name: gilgamesh-epic-standard-version
description: A scribe gathered older Sumerian tales of a king seeking immortality into the long poem that includes a great flood.

name: ashurnasirpal-builds-nimrud
description: An Assyrian king moved his capital to Kalhu and celebrated with a feast for some seventy thousand guests.

name: babylonian-astronomical-diaries
description: Priests of Babylon began systematic records of the heavens that were kept for centuries and used by later scholars.

name: tiglath-pileser-iii-reforms
description: A usurper seized the throne, reformed the army and provinces and launched a new age of Assyrian conquest.

name: sennacherib-palace-nineveh
description: An Assyrian king boasted that his Palace Without Rival was complete, with an aqueduct and gardens.

name: ashurbanipal-takes-throne
description: The last great Assyrian king succeeded his father, trained as a scribe as well as a warrior, as the empire reached its widest extent.

name: nebuchadnezzar-wins-carchemish
description: A Babylonian prince crushed the Egyptian and Assyrian remnant on the Euphrates, giving Babylon mastery of the Near East.
